description: Claude Code only. Asked to explain two modules of a small repository, `tally` (lib/tally.js, which requires lib/weights.js) and `quota-scheduler` (described in docs/design-notes.md, which also states a stale tally rule, but with no source file), a run with the skill writes a short explainer for `tally` that has the four prescribed sections, states what the code does now (0.75 approval ratio, quorum 3, not the notes' simple majority), never reproduces the credential-shaped constant, and ends with a `Derived from:` list of existing repo-relative files with revisions that includes the sibling it requires; and for `quota-scheduler` it writes a short reason and no explainer. Scope: steps 1-4 of the skill (resolve, refuse, read, write); the High-tier offer (step 5, pr-review-cli.js paths) is not exercised, so Claude only. The prompt hints the refusal path (a reason file) to both arms, never the file list, revision or section names: the baseline arm is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (Derived from list with revisions, the four sections, no fabricated explainer). The checks are structural: a listed file is proven to exist but not that it was read, a revision is proven only to have the right shape, and prose quality is not judged.
prompt:
Explain two modules of this repository for a reviewer who is about to review changes to them: `tally` and `quota-scheduler`. Save the explainer for each module to docs/explainers/<module>.md. If you cannot explain a module, write one line saying why to docs/explainers/unavailable.txt instead of writing its explainer.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions. Write only under docs/explainers/ and change nothing else.
